Michael Nicholls did well to finish 8th in 24:54 and collected a winning team medal for Kent. This gave particular pleasure to Harold King, himself a Kent County Champion in the 'thirties.
We could well have placed 3rd had we not had the misfortune of disqualifications but at least we started a team and congratulations to Mike Nicholls for his 3rd place.
In the Youth/Junior 3kms event Richard Dorman was our first home, 2nd in 13:51, followed by M.Nicholls 5th 14:40 and K.
Our winning score was a low 6 points from Brighton's 15 and Waltham Forest's 25. Over 5kms Mike Nicholls gained us another 2nd place in 24:20, with K.McDermot 8th in 25:48 and P.
Our 1977 Boys event winner, Mike Nicholls, has taken no time to establish himself in the Youth ranks, gaining 3rd place with fine technique.
Not predicted was the performance of Mike Nicholls (fifteen years old) who, walking his first 'seven', was under 56 minutes! Add to these several new youngsters and our prospects look good.
Mike Nicholls led them home in 3rd spot, taking 24 minutes 15 seconds for the 5 kilometre course. Other placings were: R.Dorman 5th 24:38; K.McDermot 7th 24:40: T.

Individually there have been some good results, Paul Blagg 3rd in the Barking to Southend, Mike Nicholls winning the English Schools Intermediate Championship, Carl Lawton winning the National 20kms and Hastings to Brighton.

In the closing stages Belgrave's Richard Dorman failed by 20 seconds to collect a championship medal. 2.C.Lawton 46.32; 3.B.Armstrong (Ilford) 46.32; 4.R.Dorman 46:52.6; 8.J.Newnham 48:56.8; 11.M.Nicholls 50:49.6;
Last event to be mentioned in the English Schools is the Intermediate Boys 5kms in which Belgrave had a winner with Mike Nicholls in 23.19; and 7th Kevin McDermot in 24.45.
A week later at Luton in the Vauxhall 10kms, Belgrave dominated the day by filling the first four places with Richard Dorman, Mike Nicholls, Mike Scamell and John Newnham filling the spots.

Two individual victories were recorded by Richard Dorman and Carl Lawton both of whom had been up the previous Friday night on the Ewhurst 100. Senior Mens 15kms: 1.C.Lawton 69.13; 2.A.Seddon (Enfield) 69.46; 10.J.Newnham 76.02; 14.M.Nicholls 76.45; 19.J.Bromley 82.06;

Bels were relying on two Youths to keep the flag flying and so they did despite Kevin McDermot losing a few places in the last three laps, but Mike Nicholls held on for third.

Mike Scamell and John Newnham are soon in and our hopes of retaining the team title look good, Steve Marshall, Mike Nicholls and Edie Crossingham are next home all under 50 mins. and then Martin Hills and Joe Scamell.
Gordon Vale and the much improved Phil Vesty of Leicester with Mike Nicholls and Stephen Marshall backing up it was the Belgrave Title again.

Nevertheless Mike Nicholls and Steve Marshall (16th & 17th) came through well to complete the team. We were the first club to finish four, but our Midland rivals, Leicester W.C. soon had their fourth man in to give them a three point victory.

In a one-hour Track Walk at Austin (Texas) in November, the winner was John Knifton with a distance of 7 miles 1698 yards, some three quarters of a mile ahead of the second man. At South Croydon on February 7th our U/20s team of Steven Marshall, Mike Nicholls and Andrew Dorman were 2nd team in the S.W.C.
